global.title: CHARTS: how the sulphuric-acid crunch is driving up critical-minerals costs
global.x: Fresh Middle-East escalation prolongs the global sulphuric-acid shortage. Spot CFR climbs above $380/t Indonesia and $440/t Chile as leach operators scramble; ~half of seaborne sulphur used to make acid is Gulf-origin. ~1/5 of world copper is acid-leach (SX-EW).

global.title: Fastmarkets launches a monthly sulphuric-acid CFR Mejillones assessment (eff. 3 Sep 2026)
global.x: A new transparent benchmark for Chilean copper operations as acid 'upends the copper market'. Platts-assessed CFR Mejillones had already doubled to $380/mt vs February.

global.title: Sulphur: Middle-East share of China's imports collapsed 56% → 20% in 2026
global.x: South Korea, Canada (Vancouver granular) and Japan fill the gap. China depends on imports for >50% of sulphur; domestic price ~CNY 8,640/t on 4 Sep. Low inventories + inelastic downstream demand keep it high and volatile.

global.title: China suspends sulphuric-acid exports — ripples through the 'sulphur–fertiliser–copper' chain
global.x: Pulling Chinese acid off the market tightens supply further for SX-EW copper leach and phosphate producers worldwide, on top of the Gulf sulphur squeeze.

global.title: Viewpoint: sulphur costs to keep ammonium-sulphate prices firm through 2026
global.x: Tampa Q1 sulphur contract seen $475–520/long tonne vs $310. Ammonia and sulphur near multi-year highs; amsul producer IOC idled then restarted on feedstock cost.

global.title: Caustic soda: US ~$358/t in June, downward pressure into H2 2026
global.x: Asian market in persistent oversupply; European chlor-alkali back from maintenance. US Gulf-Coast maintenance trimmed rates but firm Latin-American export demand and higher freight/insurance offset. Asian FOB revised up on LNG power costs.

mining.title: Copper holds near record: LME 3-month above $14,100/t, +~14% YTD
mining.x: About +47% year on year. LME stocks fell for a 42nd straight day to ~205 kt — the longest run of declines since 2014; the cash-to-3-month backwardation has eased from a mid-August peak near $550/t.

mining.title: Middle-East crisis worsens the sulphuric-acid deficit in Chilean copper mining
mining.x: Spot acid CFR Mejillones above $440/t, Indonesia above $380/t as converters scramble for alternatives. Analysts see 'no quick fix'; Fastmarkets starts a monthly Mejillones acid assessment 3 Sep.

mining.title: Zambia's copper boom draws billions in green-energy investment; DRC faces a 2,000 MW power gap
mining.x: Zambia targeting ~3 Mt/yr copper with new smelter and leach capacity — more hydromet-chemical demand. DRC's refining ambition is capped by a large power shortfall.

mining.title: Copper weekly: Codelco H1 −11%, Gresik still offline, DRC ban in month 3
mining.x: Codelco H1 output fell 11% to 564 kt on El Teniente restrictions; 2026 guidance of 1.33–1.36 Mt now 'difficult'. Indonesia's PT Smelting Gresik remains offline; the DRC concentrate export ban is in its third month.

mining.title: Analyst split: Goldman sees copper easing from record highs; Macquarie models a 2026 surplus
mining.x: Macquarie: ~262 kt surplus in 2026, then >700 kt/yr surpluses in 2027–28. A timing cue for copper-sulphate and mining-reagent demand into 2027.

mining.title: DR Congo bans exports of copper and cobalt concentrates
mining.x: Joint ministerial order signed 29 Jun 2026, immediate effect; one-year waivers possible for 'strategically important' cases; cobalt ban moving to a quota system. Congo already ships mostly refined cathode (Q1'26: 697 kt cathode vs 54 kt concentrate) — near-term copper impact limited, but the push to local hydromet/refining lifts demand for imported acid, Na₂S, metabisulphite, xanthate, MgO and copper sulphate.

africa.title: Lagos CIF caustic soda flakes $910–970/t (Sep 2026)
africa.x: Nigeria, DR Congo and Tanzania are Africa's leading caustic-soda importers by value; South Africa the largest single market (~$79M).

africa.title: Sulphuric-acid crunch raises input costs for African SX-EW and phosphate producers
africa.x: DRC and Zambia leach operations and Morocco's phosphate industry all exposed. Gulf-origin sulphur and acid rerouting around the Cape lengthens African lead times and lifts landed cost.

africa.title: Zambia pushes toward 3 Mt/yr copper with new smelter and leach capacity
africa.x: Green-energy-backed expansion lifts demand for hydromet chemicals into Zambia and the wider SADC belt; contrasts with DRC's power-constrained refining plans.

africa.title: DR Congo bans exports of copper and cobalt concentrates
africa.x: Order signed 29 Jun 2026 to force local processing. For Anatrica: more DRC domestic smelting/leach means more imported reagent demand — sulphuric acid, sodium sulphide, sodium metabisulphite, xanthate, magnesium oxide, copper sulphate — the DRC/Zambia copper-belt cluster (Tier-2 in the sourcing strategy).

africa.title: Egypt = 76% of African caustic-soda exports; net importer of liquid grade
africa.x: Egypt imports liquid caustic (~30 kt/yr from Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Russia) while exporting solid flakes to East Africa incl. Kenya — a Türkiye-FTA swing-supply lane.

africa.title: SACU keeps the 40% anti-dumping duty on US soda ash (reconfirmed 19 Feb 2026)
africa.x: Following a sunset-review application by Botswana Ash. Non-US origins (Türkiye, EU, China) are unaffected — still the live rule in South Africa / Namibia / Botswana landed cost.

mideast.title: No quick sulphuric-acid fix — ~half of the sulphur feed is Gulf-origin
mideast.x: The Gulf crunch has pushed acid CFR Chile above $440/t and Indonesia above $380/t; analysts see no near-term relief for copper leach or phosphate.

mideast.title: Gulf sulphur off the market: China's Middle-East import share fell 56% → 20%
mideast.x: Buyers shift to Canada (Vancouver), South Korea and Japan. Sulphur and downstream sulphuric acid and ammonium sulphate at record levels; ~50% of global sulphur output is Gulf, extracted from oil and gas.

mideast.title: Strait of Hormuz disruption hits fertiliser, chemical and methanol trade
mideast.x: Since 28 Feb 2026: ~one-third of seaborne methanol and roughly half of world sulphur transit the strait. Petrochemicals, fertilizers, plastics and aluminium exports from the Gulf all down; combined Gulf export volumes −54% Apr'25→Apr'26, LNG −95%.

mideast.title: Egypt leads African solid caustic-soda output; imports liquid from Saudi, Türkiye, Russia
mideast.x: Ahead of Morocco and Rwanda in solid-caustic production; a Türkiye-FTA lane for Anatrica into North and East Africa.

mideast.title: 150+ tankers anchored outside Hormuz; carriers reroute via the Cape
mideast.x: Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd suspended transits — chemical-tanker and container costs up well beyond the Gulf.

mideast.title: Aramco delays three Saudi chemical projects (Yanbu ×2 JVs, Jubail)
mideast.x: Weak oil prices curb domestic spending; major engineering and design work pushed back. COTC ambition (+10–15 Mt/yr by 2035) intact but the 2026–28 build slows.
